To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Iodine 125 implants are not effective in controlling local failure in Stage B prostatic carcinoma, but may be effective in Stage A2 prostatic carcinoma.

1) Iodine 131 implantation has no role in the definitive treatment in Stage A1 and A2 patients, but it may be appropriate for a subset of Stage B patients; 2) external beam irradiation is the preferred definitive treatment for all patients with Stage B2, C and T3 disease; 3) the complication rate is higher with external beam irradiation than with implantation.

1) the local control rate for Stage A and B patients was significantly worse for implant patients than for external beam patients; 2) the relapse-free survival rate for Stage A patients was similar for implant and external beam; 3) the relapse rate for Stage B patients was significantly lower for external beam patients than for implant patients; and 4) complication rates were similar for both groups.
